claims.text: High-entropy alloys exhibit temperature-dependent ductile–brittle transition behavior.
High-entropy alloys lose ductility within specific temperature ranges.
Phase transformations cause the proposed loss of ductility.
The proposed material is a high-entropy alloy in its as-cast state.
The alloy should be subjected to varying temperatures to observe changes in ductility.
The investigated temperatures should extend from room temperature to elevated temperatures.
Embrittlement is expected within a narrow temperature window.
Phase stability and microstructural evolution mediate the temperature-dependent mechanical response.
Elevated temperatures transform the alloy microstructure and alter the distribution of phases.
Changes in phase distribution alter ductility.
The alloy will lose ductility at specific elevated temperatures.
Ductility will recover when the alloy is returned to lower temperatures.
The transition temperature range depends on the particular high-entropy-alloy composition.
Tensile strength, fracture elongation, and microstructure can be measured across temperature to test the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted recovery is stated to occur upon returning to lower temperature, but the intervention and tensile-test design specify testing at various temperatures without an explicit heating–cooling cycle. Thus, the proposed experiment does not directly test the claimed recovery or a full ductile–brittle–ductile sequence.
